'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = U.S. senator | before_election = [[Chuck Schumer]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Chuck Schumer]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }}{{Elections in New York State}} The '''2022 United States Senate election in New York''' was held on November 8, 2022, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the [[New York (state)|State of New York]]. Incumbent four-term [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Senator [[Chuck Schumer]], who had served as [[Party leaders of the United States Senate|Senate Majority Leader]] since 2021, was first elected in 1998, defeating Republican incumbent [[Al D'Amato]]. Schumer ran for a fifth term. Republican [[Joe Pinion]] is the first black Senate nominee of any major party in New York history. The filing deadline for the June primary was April 7, 2022.{{Cite web |last=Cillizza |first=Chris |author-link=Chris Cillizza |date=April 20, 2020 |title=Does Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez have her eye on a Senate seat? |url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/04/20/politics/aoc-2022-senate-schumer/index.html |website=[[CNN Politics]]}} Schumer became the longest-serving U.S. senator in the state's history once his fifth term began in the [[118th Congress]].{{cite news |last1=Matthews |first1=Karen |last2=Hajela |first2=Deepti |title=New York's Schumer keeps Senate seat, but majority role up for grabs |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/new-yorks-schumer-keeps-senate-seat-but-majority-role-up-for-grabs/ |access-date=2022-11-09 |website=[[The Times of Israel]] |language=en-US |issn=0040-7909}} Though Schumer was comfortably re-elected by a margin of 14.01%, he lost significant support on [[Long Island]] and [[Upstate New York]] compared to [[2016 United States Senate election in New York|his last election in 2016]]. Pinion flipped the more conservative counties that Schumer had won in his previous runs, as well as some Democratic-leaning counties such as [[Nassau County, New York|Nassau]], [[Saratoga County, New York|Saratoga]], [[Broome County, New York|Broome]], [[Clinton County, New York|Clinton]], and [[Essex County, New York|Essex]]. However, Schumer's lead was large enough in [[Politics of New York City|New York City]] that most media outlets called the race in his favor the moment the polls closed.{{Cite news |last=McKinley |first=Jesse |date=2022-11-09 |title=Tough N.Y. Election Holds Lessons for Republicans and Democrats Alike |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/11/09/nyregion/ny-election-takeaways.html |access-date=2022-11-12 |issn=0362-4331}} Despite Democrats overperforming expectations on a national level during this cycle, this race was the most competitive in Schumer's Senate career since his first election in [[1998 United States Senate election in New York|1998]], when he won by 10.5%, along with being the closest U.S. Senate election from New York since [[Hillary Clinton]] won by about 12.3 percentage points in [[2000 United States Senate election in New York|2000]]. This was due to an overall Democratic underperformance in New York state despite their overperformance nationally, and Schumer's performance was still the highest margin of victory (aside from [[Thomas DiNapoli]] in the concurrent [[2022 New York State Comptroller election|comptroller election]]) on the statewide ballot. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== *[[Chuck Schumer]], incumbent U.S. senator and [[Party leaders of the United States Senate|Senate majority leader]]{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/17/nyregion/kathy-hochul-democratic-nomination.html|title = Hochul is the Star as Democrats Gather for a Cuomo-Free Convention|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date = February 17, 2022|last1 = Glueck|first1 = Katie}} ==== Disqualified ==== * Moses Mugulusi, regulator{{cite web|last=|title=Moses Mugulusi|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Moses_Mugulusi|url-status=live|website=[[Ballotpedia]]|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210911160809/https://ballotpedia.org/Moses_Mugulusi |archive-date=September 11, 2021 }} * Khaled Salem, activist{{Cite news|date=June 5, 2021|title=New York Senate candidate encourages Americans to protest Hamas|work=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|url=https://www.jpost.com/american-politics/new-york-senate-candidate-encourages-americans-to-protest-hamas-670173|url-status=live|access-date=August 30, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210829180924/https://www.jpost.com/american-politics/new-york-senate-candidate-encourages-americans-to-protest-hamas-670173|archive-date=August 29, 2021}} ==== Declined ==== *[[Alessandra Biaggi]], [[New York State Senate|state senator]] from the [[New York's 34th State Senate district|34th district]] ''([[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in New York#District 17|ran for U.S. House]])''{{Cite web|last=Murphy |first=Dan|date=2022-02-07|title=Reports: Biaggi to Announce Run for Congress in NY-3;
